name: Vaithamanidhi Perumal Temple, Thirukkolur
deity: Vishnu as Vaithamanidhi Perumal, with the Goddess Kumudavalli — the shrine of Mars (Angaraka) among the Nava Tirupati
period: A Divya Desam of the Pandya country on the Tamiraparani, sung by Nammalvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thirukkolur on the Tamiraparani, Vishnu stands as Vaithamanidhi Perumal, the lord who is himself the treasure laid in keeping — the Mars shrine among the nine planetary Tirupati, a Divya Desam sung by Nammalvar.

sections.history: Thirukkolur lies on the Tamiraparani near Alvarthirunagari, and is remembered as the home of Madhurakavi Alvar; its lord is Vaithamanidhi Perumal, honoured as the imperishable wealth entrusted to the devotee. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and one of the Nava Tirupati — the nine temples of the Tamiraparani, each held as a planetary shrine of the Vaishnavas. Among the Nava Tirupati it is honoured as the shrine of Mars, Angaraka.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner of the Pandya country and its later patrons, the temple is entered through a gateway tower and gathered around the sanctum of the presiding Vishnu, with the Goddess in her own shrine. Here the lord is worshipped as Vaithamanidhi Perumal, with the Goddess Kumudavalli. Pillared halls open before the sanctum, in the temple manner of the deep south.
sections.legends: The Nava Tirupati are worshipped together as the nine planetary shrines of the Vaishnavas: where the Shaiva tradition of the Kaveri keeps nine separate Navagraha temples, here the nine planets are honoured across the nine abodes of Vishnu on the Tamiraparani, all sung by Nammalvar, the foremost of the Alvars, whose own birthplace is Alvarthirunagari among them. At Thirukkolur the planet is Mars, Angaraka.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the great Vaishnava festivals — Vaikunta Ekadashi, the Garuda Sevai when the nine are worshipped in a single round, and the days of Nammalvar and the Alvars — with processions through the riverside villages. The Tamiraparani's own festivals draw the surrounding country.
sections.experience: A quiet riverside Divya Desam among the nine, rewarding for the pilgrim who follows the Tamiraparani from one Tirupati to the next. As the shrine of Mars, it takes its place in the single pilgrimage of the Nava Tirupati that gathers the nine planets into the abodes of Vishnu.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Garuda Sevai and Vaikunta Ekadashi days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: It lies in the Tirunelveli–Thoothukudi country on the Tamiraparani, on the Tirunelveli–Tiruchendur route, reachable by road from Tirunelveli; the nine Tirupati villages lie close together along the river.
